6.text: The people of the Pacific villages continue to go every year with dog-

7.text: teams to the Russian settlements on the Anadyr, because the route to that

8.text: point is much shorter than to the Anui. The best place for meeting is not

9.text: at the fairs mentioned above, but in the neighborhood of the mouth of the

10.text: Anadyr, whither the journey from the nearest Chukchee village, across Holy

11.text: Cross Bay, can be made, in the spring of the year, in five or six days. For

12.text: half a century the meeting-place has been on the tundra, twenty miles north-

13.text: ward from the mouth of the Anadyr, near the Hare Mountains; but for the

14.text: last ten years two small fairs have been arranged instead at Mariinsky Post, —

15.text: one in the spring, and the other in the summer, about the time of the arrival

16.text: of the mail-steamer. In the spring about fifty dog-sledges come from the Chuk-

17.text: chee and Eskimo villages as far as Indian Point, and about twice as many

18.text: reindeer-sledges from the Oˊnmɪlɪn and Telqäˊp camps. In summer ten or

19.text: fifteen skin boats from the same maritime villages, a few boats of the Telqäˊp

20.text: Reindeer Chukchee, and even some of the Kerek, visit the port.

21.text: TOBACCO AND BRICK-TEA. — Of all Russian wares, tobacco held the first

22.text: place. The craving of the natives for it is aptly expressed in a tale well

23.text: known to all tribes of northeastern Siberia.

24.text: In the time of a tobacco famine, when all the people were nearly mad

25.text: because they had nothing to smoke, one well-to-do reindeer-breeder possessed

26.text: a large pouch quite filled with tobacco, but would not share it with any one.

27.text: At last his own brother asked for a pipeful, and was refused. The next day

28.text: he overtook the owner of the tobacco on the tundra, stabbed him from behind

29.text: with his spear, ripped open his breast, and took out his lungs, which he found

30.text: covered with soot. He scraped away a part of this, and used it to fill his

31.text: pipe. The pouch he left untouched. When caught by the Cossacks and

32.text: brought before the Russian magistrate, he showed him the big pouch and the

33.text: sooty lungs, and was acquitted of the charge.

34.text: Tobacco has found its way from Siberia far eastward into arctic America.

39.text: rustling, the parts come together, and they dive into the water. These, too,
